title: Degree-zero compact-support vanishing for an ordinary middle extension
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-wf-middle-extension]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ with chosen coefficient field $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $C_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve over $k_0$, meaning a separated finite-type affine $k_0$-scheme whose structure morphism is smooth of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and whose base change to every field extension of $k_0$ is connected. Let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a dense open immersion and let $\mathcal F_0$ be a lisse $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil sheaf on $U_0$ in the finite-extension adic convention of [def-wf-middle-extension], with Weil structure as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Put $C=C_0\times_{k_0}k$ and write $j:U\hookrightarrow C$ and $\mathcal F$ for the geometric base changes. Write $j_*\mathcal F$ for the ordinary sheaf direct image of [def-wf-middle-extension], placed in degree zero, rather than the full complex $Rj_*\mathcal F$; it is a constructible sheaf on $C$ by [lem-a1-adic-middle-extension-constructible], so its compact-support cohomology is defined. In the completed integral, rationalized, common-finite-stage compact-support convention of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], after forgetting the Weil structure, one has
$$H_c^0(C,j_*\mathcal F)=0.$$
No purity, weight, or ramification condition on $\mathcal F_0$ is required.

proof.text: Write $C_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$; then $C=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_{k_0}k)$ by the affine fibre-product construction, so $C$ is affine. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $C$ is separated and of finite type over $k$. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1), its structure map is smooth of relative dimension one. Geometric connectedness in the statement gives that $C$ is nonempty and connected. Thus [lem-sbc-smooth-fixed-dimension-over-field] gives $\dim C=1$. These verify all the smooth connected curve hypotheses used below.

proof.text: The affine geometric curve cannot be proper: proper and affine would imply dimension at most zero, contradicting its smooth dimension one. If a closed subset Z proper over the base were the whole curve, apply the universal closed-subscheme characterization to the identity immersion to make the structure morphism proper. Thus every such Z is different from the whole curve. This uses no reduced-induced-subscheme identification.

source.place: Remark 29.7, p. 166, nonproperness in the support argument; proper closed subset convention: Stacks coherent.tex, Tags 0CYM/0CYL, and schemes.tex, Tag 01J4

proof.text: The actual ordinary image belongs to the common-stage heart by its constructibility declaration. Apply the degree-zero proper-support comparison. Each compact class produces a section of the ordinary image which vanishes outside some closed subset Z proper over the geometric field. The preceding step makes the complementary open nonempty. Apply unique continuation of ordinary middle-extension sections to this open: the compared section is zero.

source.place: Definition 18.1 and Proposition 18.3(b), pp. 118–121; the cited constructible-section comparison explicitly supplies the adic extension and compatibility with lisse realization; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15

proof.text: The section comparison is an isomorphism onto ordinary degree-zero Hom sections, and the compact-to-ordinary comparison is injective. Hence any two compact classes have equal images and are equal. Transport this equality through the recorded compact-value isomorphism, cancel its inverse and the universe lift. This proves Subsingleton for exactly the displayed cohomology group, for every compactification and the given induced Weil structure.

Steps 5-7 hold. lem-a1-constructible-degree-zero-proper-support supplies injective alpha, a proper Z and compatibility with open restriction. Faithfulness of the fibre functor in cor-galois-lisse-representations(2) at a point of U minus Z gives t=0, and restriction from C to U is injective on sections of ordinary j_*F, so c=0.
